record.question: Major causes of floods in India are:
record.explanation: Standard Indian geography texts (e.g. the NCERT Class 11 'Floods' section) rank prolonged, intense monsoon rainfall as the principal cause of floods in India, with the Ganga-Brahmaputra and other basins flooding from long spells of heavy rain; tropical cyclones and cloud bursts are only localized/seasonal contributors (coastal storm surges and Himalayan flash floods), 'large catchment areas' is a physical aggravator of flood peaks rather than a cause, and inadequate drainage explains urban waterlogging rather than riverine flooding. Note the item is poorly discriminating: heavy rainfall, tropical cyclones/cloud bursts and insufficient drainage are all genuine contributing causes, so the choice of the dominant one is a judgment call, hence medium confidence.
